name: @capital-q/q-connectors
description: Where Q's typed tools meet the outside protocols (doc 12 §34-§35): Q as an MCP client, where an approved remote tool becomes a source-controlled Capital Q tool with its own Zod input and output, its own authorize step and the Tool Registry's policy; Q as a constrained MCP server façade, where a compatible host reaches only the tools the registry offers the authenticated person, through the same execution pipeline; and the LangChain projection of the registry, so a graph node calls a Capital Q tool as data. No connector holds a credential in code, no remote tool is trusted because it answered, and nothing here bypasses authorization.
